root_cause.text: In `bpf_jit_prog_release_other()` the BPF JIT constant-blinding clone replacement updated `aux->prog` but forgot to update `aux->offload->prog` for dev-bound-only XDP programs, leaving a stale pointer to a freed `struct bpf_prog` that later gets dereferenced during netns cleanup.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (fp->aux->offload) fp->aux->offload->prog = fp;` immediately after `fp->aux->prog = fp;`, and the CVE description says `bpf_jit_blind_constants()` clones the program, the original is freed in `bpf_jit_prog_release_other()`, but `offload->prog` is left pointing to the freed original and is later used by `__bpf_prog_offload_destroy(offload->prog)` in `bpf_dev_bound_netdev_unregister()`.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds `if (fp->aux->offload) fp->aux->offload->prog = fp;` immediately after `fp->aux->prog = fp;`, and the CVE description says `bpf_jit_blind_constants()` clones the program, the original is freed in `bpf_jit_prog_release_other()`, but `offload->prog` is left pointing to the freed original and is later used by `__bpf_prog_offload_destroy(offload->prog)` in `bpf_dev_bound_netdev_unregister()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update the offload program backreference to the surviving BPF program when releasing the other clone.
intent_record.what: In bpf_jit_prog_release_other(), after assigning fp->aux->prog = fp;, the code now also checks whether fp->aux->offload is present and, if so, assigns fp->aux->offload->prog = fp; before calling bpf_prog_clone_free(fp_other).
intent_record.how: This ensures that any offload-side backreference to the program is updated to point at fp when the clone/original relationship is resolved, keeping the offload metadata consistent and preventing it from still referencing the soon-to-be-freed fp_other.

grouping_result.intent: Update the offload program backreference to the surviving BPF program when releasing the other clone.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it updates the offload program backreference to point to the surviving BPF program, fixing the stale `aux->offload->prog` pointer left behind during clone replacement.

candidates.rationale: This updates only the main auxiliary backreference to the surviving clone, but the root cause says the offload backreference was left stale; the missing corresponding update to aux->offload->prog can leave a freed prog pointer behind.
Freeing the other clone is what makes any unreplaced backreference dangerous; if aux->offload->prog still points to fp_other, later dereference during cleanup becomes a use-after-free.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement only updates the main auxiliary backreference to the surviving BPF program. Per the root cause, the corresponding offload backreference for dev-bound-only XDP programs was not updated, leaving aux->offload->prog stale and able to point to freed memory after the clone is released.

Freeing the replaced clone makes the stale offload backreference unsafe if it was not updated first. Because aux->offload->prog can still reference fp_other, this free enables the later use-after-free during netns cleanup.
